stem.text: The electron micrograph shows some of the airways in the gaseous exchange system of an insect and the respiring body cells that surround them.

stem.alt: Electron micrograph of branching tubular airways among cells, with printed labels for respiring body cell, trachea, spiracles, chitin and tracheoles.

stem.text: Which statements describe correct differences between the insect gas exchange system shown in the electron micrograph and the human gas exchange system?

items: Gas exchange occurs through the walls of the airways directly into respiring body cells in insects but this does **not** occur in humans.
There are spirals of chitin in the walls of a trachea in insects to hold it open but **not** in humans.
There is more than one trachea in the gas exchange system of the insect but only one in humans.
